svg.title: A six-stage flowchart of the collaboration cycle between teacher, parent and specialist, running from finding out who actually raises the child, through going to the family in their own language about something good, asking four named questions and recording the answers, agreeing one change each plus a non-literate communication channel, writing a one-page shared support plan the class teacher holds, and finally a specialist visit ordered as watch-then-plan-then-brief-work rather than a handover, with return arrows for termly revisiting and for a failed channel, a side box listing the team available when no specialist exists, and a footer noting classroom changes can begin immediately while visits and information sharing need agreement.
svg.desc: A six-stage flowchart of the collaboration cycle between teacher, parent and specialist, running from finding out who actually raises the child, through going to the family in their own language about something good, asking four named questions and recording the answers, agreeing one change each plus a non-literate communication channel, writing a one-page shared support plan the class teacher holds, and finally a specialist visit ordered as watch-then-plan-then-brief-work rather than a handover, with return arrows for termly revisiting and for a failed channel, a side box listing the team available when no specialist exists, and a footer noting classroom changes can begin immediately while visits and information sharing need agreement.
svg.text: Collaboration: one term, two afternoons, a
borrowed phone
1. Who actually raises this child?
Ask the child, not only the register: mother,
grandmother, aunt or elder brother. A father
recorded in the register may be away in
Karachi.
2. Go to them in their language
Begin with something the child can do. If a
visit is impossible, use a trusted messenger.
Do not rely on an unread note; never make
first contact a complaint.
3. Ask four questions; record answers
What at home makes you proud?
How do you gain attention, and how does she
signal not understanding?
What is hardest at school?
What should she do by year’s end?
4. One change each, and a channel
Teacher changes one thing on Monday. Family
does one free thing needing no reading. Agree
a voice note, relative’s phone or older cousin
as messenger.
5. A one-page shared support plan
What are we trying for? Who does what? How
will we know? Class teacher holds the page. If
no specialist: ask head, last year’s teacher,
Lady Health Worker, family, child and class.
6. Specialist, if and when available
Watch class first; plan with teacher second;
work with child briefly third. Never a
handover.
Each term: return to the four questions; answers
change.
If nothing comes back, revisit the channel, not
blame the family.
Begin classroom changes; agree visits, information
sharing and outside support with family and school.
